scope: Static publication/software-documentation provenance only. No solver execution, no protected-result opening, no Level-B change, no Korkin-gate authorization.

target.paper: Korkin et al. (2022), Numerical results for polarized light scattering in a spherical atmosphere
target.case: multiple scattering, uniform layer, OT=0.25, cos(SZA)=0.1

newEvidence.claim: The official MYSTIC output documentation distinguishes plain monochromatic files from calibrated .spc output. Plain mc.rad is radiance output without extraterrestrial-irradiance, Sun-Earth-distance, spectral-integration or related calibration factors; the monochromatic files are explicitly described as transmittances of the form E/E0, L/E0, etc. The guide separately defines reflectivity as pi*L/(E0*cos(SZA)), so the documented plain-radiance convention is not silently a pi-scaled reflectivity convention.
newEvidence.consequence: The native plain monochromatic MYSTIC radiance convention is fixed as L/E0-family output rather than an unknown pi-scaled quantity.

newEvidence.claim: The manuscript's table dictionary states that MYSTIC: I is the total intensity I computed with the Monte Carlo RT code MYSTIC; it likewise identifies OMC: I Q U P in the supplementary-file description as the full-spherical model and later calls the MYSTIC full-spherical result the baseline.
newEvidence.consequence: Table 9(a) is directly tied to a MYSTIC-computed intensity, not an independently defined observational radiance scale.

newEvidence.claim: Table 9(a) is explicitly the multiple-scattering uniform-layer OT=0.25, cos(SZA)=0.1 benchmark and reports MYSTIC: I alongside MCSSA and VLIDORT comparisons.
newEvidence.consequence: The frozen V32 benchmark identity is author-side and exact.

resolvedFacts.nativePlainMysticRadianceConvention: L/E0-family monochromatic transmittance; not pi*L/(E0*cos(SZA)) reflectivity
resolvedFacts.korkinTable9QuantityIdentity: MYSTIC total intensity I computed with MYSTIC
resolvedFacts.benchmarkIdentity: Table 9(a), multiple scattering, uniform layer, OT=0.25, cos(SZA)=0.1
